texts.preamble: Sanjeev Kumar vs Food Safety Officer on 17 February, 2020 In The Court Of Sh. Dinesh Kumar Sharma District & Sessions Judge / Appellate Tribunal, Phc, New Delhi In the matter of : Fsat No. 12/2019 1. Sanjeev Kumar S/o Sh. Ram Kishan 1573, Gali No. 3 Bagh Ramanand Amritsar-143 006 2. M/s Amar Singh Chawal Wala Outside Chattiwing Gate Amritsar-143 006
texts.facts: The facts in brief are that on 16.03.2017, Sh. Som Pal Singh, Food Safety Officer purchased the sample of Lal Quilla "Basmati Rice", an article of food for analysis under the provisions of The Food Safety & Standards Act/Rules/Regulations, from Sh. Rajeev Gupta S/o Sh. B.B. Gupta, M/s Gupta Provision Store, Shop No. 12, Ram Dwara Road, Pahar Ganj, Delhi-110 055. 3. The necessary procedure was followed and the sample was sent to Food Analyst. The Food Analyst vide report dated 23.03.2017, inter alia , opined that the sample was misbranded because of violation of Regulation No. 2.2.1(3) read with 2.3.1(5) of The Food Safety & Standards (Packaging & Sanjeev Kumar vs Food Safety Officer on 17 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83394065/ 1 Lebelling) Regulation, 2011. 4. The complaint was filed with the Adjudicating Officer, who held the appellant guilty and imposed penalty of Rs.40,000/- and also directed to remove the words "2 years" from the package. 5. The appellant has challenged the impugned order predominantly on the ground that the contention of the appellant was rejected in arbitrary manner without seeing the record and also the report of the Food Analyst. It has further been submitted that the application moved by the appellant to summon an expert agricultural scientist Mr. A.K. Singh from Indian Agricultural Research Institute, Pusa was also rejected.
texts.arguments: 6. Sh. R.K. Ahuja, Ld. Counsel for the appellant, during the course of arguments, submitted that the Adjudicating Officer did not follow the procedure and held the appellant guilty without any material on record. 7. Per contra, Sh. Kundan Lal, Ld. Sr. PP for the State/respondent submitted that the Adjudicating Officer had given a reasonable opportunity to the appellant and, therefore, there is no illegality or infirmity in the order of the Adjudicating Officer. He has further submitted that it was for the appellant to prove on record that the claims made by them were true and correct. He has invited attention of the Court to Regulation No. 2.2.1(3) read with 2.3.1(5) of The Food Safety & Standards (Packaging & Lebelling) Regulation, 2011, which are as under: Regulation No. 2.2.1(3) "Pre-packaged food shall not be described or presented on any label or in any labelling manner that is false, misleading or deceptive or is likely to create an erroneous impression regarding its character in any respect." Regulation No. 2.3.1(5) "Labels not to contain false or misleading statements: A label shall not contain any statement, claim, design, device, fancy name or abbreviation which is false or misleading in any particular concerning the food contained in the package, or concerning the quantity or the nutritive value or in relation to the place of origin of the said food: Provided that this regulation shall not apply in respect of established trade or fancy names of confectionery, biscuits and sweets, such as, barley, sugar, bull's eye, cream cracker or in respect of aerated waters, such as, Ginger Beer or Gold-Spot or any other name in existence in international trade practice." 8. Ld. Sr. PP for the State/respondent submitted that under The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, there is no need for the prosecution to prove intention and if there is violation of the Act, the appellant is liable to be punished. Perusal of Section 68(2) would indicate that the Adjudicating Officer is liable to give reasonable opportunity for making representation in the matter, and if, on such inquiry, he is satisfied that the person has committed the contravention of provisions of this Act or the rules or the regulations made thereunder, the penalty may be imposed. Section 68(3) confers power of a Civil Court upon the Adjudicating Officer.
